Reference › Error codes

Error codes

Pare only erases types: it replaces type syntax with spaces and changes nothing else, so every line and column of the output matches the source. TypeScript syntax that would need new JavaScript written in its place cannot be erased, so Pare rejects it instead of guessing. This is the rule behind TypeScript's erasableSyntaxOnly option and Node's built-in type stripping: turning on erasableSyntaxOnly in tsconfig.json makes tsc and the editor report the PARE100 to PARE105 cases as TS1294. Pare also rejects parameter decorators (PARE106), which that option allows.

A rejected file gets no output. The CLI exits with 1, the MSBuild package fails the build, and AddPareDevelopment logs the error and keeps the previous .js. Every rejection in a file is reported in one run.

Code Kind Message
PARE001 error syntax error
PARE100 error 'enum' generates runtime code and cannot be erased
PARE101 error namespace containing values generates runtime code
PARE102 error parameter property generates runtime code
PARE103 error 'import x = ...' generates runtime code
PARE104 error 'export =' is CommonJS-only emit
PARE105 error angle-bracket type assertion is not supported
PARE106 error parameter decorators need legacy experimentalDecorators
PARE107 error a type-only import cannot have both a default and named bindings
PARE200 warning (MSBuild) not served: the build now writes this file's output under obj/ and serves that. Delete it.
PARE201 error (MSBuild) two sources map to one URL
PARE202 warning (MSBuild) not served: outside wwwroot with no PareServeAt
PARE203 error (MSBuild) PareServeAt is not a URL folder
PARE204 error (MSBuild) PareCompileSource needs PareCompiler and PareOutputExtension
PARE205 error (MSBuild) a source outside the project folder cannot be written below PareOutDir

Errors print as file:line:col: error PARE100: message (hint) from the CLI and the hot-reload watcher, and as file(line,col): error PARE100: message (hint) from MSBuild.

PARE001

syntax error (check the syntax at this position)

The input is not valid TypeScript at this position. Pare stops at the first syntax error; the position is the token where parsing failed. Nesting too deep for the parser's stack (thousands of levels) is reported the same way rather than crashing. .tsx and JSX are not supported.

ts 
let total = ;

Fix the syntax:

ts 
let total = 0;

PARE100

'enum' generates runtime code and cannot be erased (use a 'const' object with 'as const' instead of 'enum')

An enum compiles to an object built at run time, so it cannot be erased. const enum is rejected too: tsc inlines its members at each use, which an eraser cannot do. declare enum emits nothing and is erased.

ts 
enum Color { Red, Green }

Use an object with as const, and a type of the same name for its values:

ts 
const Color = { Red: 0, Green: 1 } as const;
type Color = (typeof Color)[keyof typeof Color];
let c: Color = Color.Red;

PARE101

namespace containing values generates runtime code (use an ES module instead of a namespace)

A namespace or module block that declares values (variables, functions, classes, nested namespaces with values) compiles to an object built at run time. A namespace that holds only types, or one marked declare, is erased.

ts 
namespace Util {
  export const version = 1;
}

Use a module: export the values from the file, and keep namespaces for types only:

ts 
export const version = 1;
namespace Shapes {
  export type Kind = "circle" | "square";
}
let k: Shapes.Kind = "circle";

PARE102

parameter property generates runtime code (declare the field in the class body and assign it in the constructor)

A constructor parameter with public, private, protected, readonly or override also declares a field and assigns it, which needs code that is not in the source.

ts 
class Point {
  constructor(public x: number) {}
}

Declare the field and assign it yourself:

ts 
class Point {
  x: number;
  constructor(x: number) {
    this.x = x;
  }
}

PARE103

'import x = ...' generates runtime code (use an ES 'import' declaration)

import x = require("m") is CommonJS emit, and import x = N.y creates a variable. import type x = require("m") is erased.

ts 
import fs = require("node:fs");

Use an ES import, or import type when only types are used:

ts 
import fs from "node:fs";
import type Fs = require("node:fs");

PARE104

'export =' is CommonJS-only emit (use 'export default' instead)

export = compiles to module.exports = ..., which has no ES module form.

ts 
function greet() {}
export = greet;
ts 
function greet() {}
export default greet;

PARE105

angle-bracket type assertion is not supported (use 'expr as T' instead of '<T>expr')

<T>expr is the older assertion form. It reads like JSX and is not allowed in .tsx files, so Pare accepts only the as form, which every TypeScript file can use.

ts 
declare const input: unknown;
let n = <number>input;
ts 
declare const input: unknown;
let n = input as number;

PARE106

parameter decorators need legacy experimentalDecorators (use TC39 decorators on the class or member instead)

Decorators on parameters exist only in TypeScript's legacy experimentalDecorators mode, whose emit rewrites the class. Standard (TC39) decorators on classes and members are kept as written; the runtime has to support them.

ts 
declare function log(target: object, key: string, index: number): void;
class Api {
  get(@log id: string) {}
}

Decorate the method instead:

ts 
declare function log(value: Function, context: ClassMethodDecoratorContext): void;
class Api {
  @log
  get(id: string) {}
}

PARE107

a type-only import cannot have both a default and named bindings (split it into two 'import type' declarations)

TypeScript rejects this form too (TS1363).

ts 
import type Config, { Options } from "./config.ts";
ts 
import type Config from "./config.ts";
import type { Options } from "./config.ts";

PARE200

warning PARE200: not served: the build now writes this file's output under obj/ and serves that. Delete it.

MSBuild package only, for web projects whose output goes under obj/ (the default since 0.3). A foo.js sits next to foo.ts in wwwroot: left there by Pare 0.2, which wrote output next to the source, or written by hand. The build serves and publishes the stripped foo.ts from obj/ and leaves foo.js out, so the two cannot conflict. The same holds for another compiler's output (App.svelte.js next to App.svelte). The build still succeeds.

Delete the foo.js files the warning names, and any .gitignore rules added for them. If a hand-written foo.js is the one you want served, rename it or the .ts.

PARE201

error PARE201: two sources map to one URL, js/app.js: wwwroot/js/app.ts, Scripts/app.ts. Serve one under a different PareServeAt folder, or remove one from its item.

MSBuild package only, for web projects whose output goes under obj/. Each source's output is served at a URL: its path below wwwroot by default, or below the folder its PareServeAt names. Two sources ended up with the same one, which would also make them write the same file. The sources of another compiler (PareCompileSource) count too, so a .svelte and a .ts cannot share a URL. Paths that differ only in case count as the same, as they do on macOS and Windows file systems. The build stops before stripping anything.

Give one of the named sources a different PareServeAt, or exclude one of them from TypeScriptSource (<TypeScriptSource Remove="Scripts/app.ts" />) or PareCompileSource.

PARE202

warning PARE202: not served: outside wwwroot with no PareServeAt, so the .js goes next to the source and is not a static web asset. Add PareServeAt="js" to its item to serve it under js/, or add PARE202 to NoWarn to keep it as is.

MSBuild package only, for web projects whose output goes under obj/. A TypeScriptSource (or PareCompileSource) item outside wwwroot, such as Scripts/app.ts, has no PareServeAt. Its output is written next to it, as Scripts/app.js, which the web app does not serve or publish. The build still succeeds. Not reported for PareOutDir, outside web projects, or for a .razor.ts or .cshtml.ts, whose output beside the component the SDK serves itself.

To serve it, name the URL folder:

XML 
<TypeScriptSource Include="Scripts/**/*.ts" PareServeAt="js" />

To keep the output next to the source on purpose, add <NoWarn>$(NoWarn);PARE202</NoWarn> to the project.

PARE203

error PARE203: PareServeAt="js/app.js" is not a URL folder. Give a folder such as js, or / for the root, with no . or .. segment, colon, double slash or file name: the file name comes from the source.

MSBuild package only. PareServeAt names a folder; each file's name and extension come from its source (app.ts gives app.js, app.mts gives app.mjs). Values with a . or .. segment, a colon, // (or \\), or ending in a script extension such as .js or .ts are rejected. The build stops before stripping anything.

Use a folder: PareServeAt="js", or PareServeAt="/" to serve at the root of the project's static web assets.

PARE204

error PARE204: PareCompileSource needs PareCompiler (the compiler's name: letters, digits, . _ -) and PareOutputExtension (the output's extension, a dot and a name such as .svelte.js); got PareCompiler="husk" PareOutputExtension="svelte.js".

MSBuild package only. A package that compiles another language to JavaScript (see Compiling other languages) declared a PareCompileSource item without a PareCompiler made of letters, digits, ., _ and -, or without a PareOutputExtension that starts with a dot and holds no folder or quote. The build stops before compiling anything. This is a fault in that package's .props or in the project file that added the item:

XML 
<PareCompileSource Include="Components/**/*.svelte" PareCompiler="husk" PareOutputExtension=".svelte.js" />

PARE205

error PARE205: the source is outside the project folder, so its output would be written outside PareOutDir="gen". Move the source into the project, or build it from the project that owns it.

MSBuild package only. PareOutDir mirrors each source's path below the project folder. A TypeScriptSource such as ../shared/x.ts has no such path: the output would have gone to shared/x.js above the project, not under gen/. The build stops before writing anything.

XML 
<PropertyGroup><PareOutDir>gen</PareOutDir></PropertyGroup>
<ItemGroup><TypeScriptSource Include="../shared/x.ts" /></ItemGroup> <!-- PARE205 -->

Without PareOutDir the output sits next to the source, as before.
